title: Who can read what
subtitle: Everything is encrypted before it leaves your machine. The line stops being where the data is stored and becomes who holds the keys.
alt: Two zones. On your machine: your files, and the keys, which stay with you. An arrow, encrypted before it leaves your machine, to the server, which holds ciphertext and nothing else: not your filenames, not your directory structure, not your commit messages. One object is 786 bytes of AES-256-GCM ciphertext named by the SHA-256 of the encrypted bytes, so the host can deduplicate it, cache it for a year and serve it from a CDN while remaining unable to tell you what it is. A note: there is no key escrow, no admin override and no support engineer who can recover it for you.
